question: What is the minimum and maximum length of an Erasmus+ study period abroad?
answer:
The duration of an Erasmus+ study period depends on the type of mobility you choose:

*   **Long-term mobility (standard):** From **2 months** (or one academic term or trimester) to **12 months** of physical mobility (Programme Guide 2026, p. 53).
*   **Short-term blended mobility:** Between **5 days and 30 days** of physical mobility. This type must be combined with a compulsory virtual component (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).
*   **Doctoral mobility:** From **5 to 30 days** or from **2 to 12 months** of physical mobility (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).

**Important limits:**
*   **Maximum per cycle:** You can participate in mobility periods totalling up to **12 months** maximum per study cycle (Bachelor, Master, or Doctorate), regardless of the number or type of mobilities (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).
*   **One-cycle degrees:** In programmes such as Medicine, the maximum duration is extended to **24 months** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).

question: ¿Cuántos meses de Erasmus puedo hacer en total durante el grado?
answer:
Puedes realizar un máximo de **12 meses** de movilidad física por cada ciclo de estudios (Grado, Máster o Doctorado) (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).

Aquí tienes los detalles importantes sobre esta duración:

*   **Suma de movilidades:** El límite de 12 meses es el total acumulado por ciclo, independientemente del número de movilidades que hagas o de si son para estudios o para prácticas (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).
*   **Experiencia previa:** Si ya has participado antes en el programa Erasmus+ (o Erasmus Mundus), ese tiempo se descuenta de los 12 meses disponibles para tu grado actual (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).
*   **Prácticas para recién graduados:** Si decides hacer prácticas Erasmus justo después de terminar el grado, esos meses también cuentan dentro del límite de 12 meses de tu ciclo de grado (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).
*   **Excepción para grados de ciclo largo:** En carreras de un solo ciclo, como Medicina, el límite total se amplía hasta los **24 meses** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).

Para conocer los plazos de solicitud y el número de plazas disponibles en tu caso concreto, debes consultar con la oficina de relaciones internacionales de tu universidad.

question: I study medicine, which is a one-cycle programme. How long can I be mobile with Erasmus+?
answer:
In one-cycle study programmes, such as medicine, you can be mobile for up to **24 months** in total (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54, Note 67).

Here are the specific details regarding this duration:
*   **Total limit:** While the standard limit for other degrees is 12 months per study cycle, one-cycle programmes have a higher limit of 24 months (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).
*   **Prior experience:** Any previous participation in the Erasmus+ programme or as an Erasmus Mundus scholarship holder during the same cycle counts towards this 24-month maximum (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54, Note 66).
*   **Types of mobility:** This total includes all types of physical mobility, whether for studies or traineeships (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).
*   **Individual mobility duration:** Each individual study mobility must last between 2 and 12 months, and each traineeship must also last between 2 and 12 months (Programme Guide 2026, p. 53).

question: Can recent graduates do an Erasmus+ traineeship, and by when must they finish it?
answer:
Yes, recent graduates can participate in Erasmus+ traineeships, provided they meet specific timing requirements:

*   **Selection:** You must be selected by your higher education institution during your **last year of study** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 55).
*   **Completion:** You must carry out and complete your traineeship abroad **within one year (12 months)** of your graduation (Programme Guide 2026, p. 55).
*   **Duration limits:** The time spent on a recent graduate traineeship counts towards the maximum limit of 12 months of mobility allowed for the study cycle in which you applied (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).
*   **Exceptions:** In countries where graduates must perform obligatory military or civil service after graduation, the one-year eligibility period is extended by the duration of that service (Programme Guide 2026, p. 48, Note 62).

Please note that your university (the beneficiary organisation) has the right to opt out of offering traineeships for recent graduates, so you should check with your international office if they participate in this specific type of mobility (Programme Guide 2026, p. 55).

question: Can I do a short stay abroad instead of a full semester? How long must the stay be?
answer:
Yes, you can do a short stay instead of a full semester through **blended short-term mobility** or **short-term doctoral mobility**.

The duration requirements are:

*   **Blended short-term mobility:** The physical stay must last between **5 and 30 days** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54). This option is available to any student, especially those unable to participate in long-term mobility, and it **must** be combined with a compulsory virtual component (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54; Learning Agreement guidelines, "Learning agreement types and mobility duration").
*   **Short-term doctoral mobility:** Doctoral candidates can also carry out a physical stay of **5 to 30 days**, but for them, the virtual component is optional (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54; Learning Agreement guidelines, "Learning agreement types and mobility duration").
*   **Standard long-term mobility:** If you choose a traditional study or traineeship period (like a full semester), the minimum duration is **2 months** or one academic term/trimester (Programme Guide 2026, p. 53).

For a blended short-term mobility for studies to be eligible, it must award a minimum of **3 ECTS credits** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).

passages.text: This higher education mobility action supports physical and blended mobility of higher education students in any study field and cycle (short cycle, bachelor, master and doctoral levels). Students can either study abroad at a partner higher education institution or carry out a traineeship in an enterprise, a research institute, a laboratory, an organisation or any other relevant workplace abroad. Students can also combine a study period abroad with a traineeship, further enhancing the learning outcomes and development of transversal skills. While long-term physical mobility is strongly encouraged, this action recognises the need to offer more flexible physical mobility duration to ensure the Programme is accessible to students from all backgrounds, circumstances and study fields. This action also supports higher education teaching and administrative staff to take part in professional development activities abroad as well as staff from the world of work to teach and train students or staff at higher education institutions. These activities may consist of teaching as well as training periods (such as job shadowing, observation periods, training courses). Furthermore, this action supports blended intensive programmes, allowing for groups of higher education institutions to jointly develop blended mobility curricula and activities for students as well as academic and administrative staff.

question: What is the minimum number of ECTS credits a blended mobility for studies must award?
answer:
A blended mobility for studies must award a minimum of **3 ECTS credits** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).

This requirement applies to:

*   **Blended Intensive Programmes (BIPs):** The combined virtual and physical components must award at least 3 ECTS credits for students (Programme Guide 2026, p. 58, 59).

question: Does my Erasmus+ study period have to be part of my degree?
answer:
Yes, the study period abroad must be part of your study programme to complete a degree (Programme Guide 2026, p. 48, 55).

The official rules state:
*   **Degree Requirement:** You must be enrolled in a higher education institution in studies leading to a recognized degree or tertiary level qualification (Programme Guide 2026, p. 55).
*   **Integration:** The study period abroad must be part of your study programme to complete that degree at any study cycle (Programme Guide 2026, p. 48).
*   **Recognition:** The Learning Agreement you sign before leaving is the basis for ensuring the automatic recognition of your mobility period, meaning the credits you earn abroad must count toward your home degree (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period").

If you have questions about which specific courses from your degree can be taken abroad, you should contact your home university's international office or your academic coordinator.

question: How much extra per month do students on an Erasmus+ traineeship receive?
answer:
Students and recent graduates carrying out an Erasmus+ traineeship receive a top-up of **150 EUR per month** in addition to their individual support grant (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68).

Here are the specific details regarding this supplement:

*   **Combination with other top-ups:** If you are a student with fewer opportunities, you are entitled to receive both the "fewer opportunities" top-up and the traineeship top-up (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68).
*   **Short-term mobility:** This traineeship top-up does **not** apply to short-term physical mobility (such as blended mobility or doctoral short-term mobility) (Programme Guide 2026, p. 70).
*   **International mobility:** For mobility to most third countries not associated with the Programme (Regions 1-12), the grant is a fixed amount (e.g., 700 EUR per month) and the traineeship top-up does not apply in the same way as it does for European countries (Programme Guide 2026, p. 69).

The exact total amount of your grant depends on your home country and the destination country, as National Agencies set the base amounts within specific ranges (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68). You should check with your university's international office for the specific rates applicable to your situation.

question: How much individual support do I get per day on a short-term physical mobility?
answer:
For a short-term physical mobility, the base amounts for individual support are:

*   **79 EUR per day** up to the 14th day of activity (Programme Guide 2026, p. 69).
*   **56 EUR per day** from the 15th to the 30th day of activity (Programme Guide 2026, p. 70).

These base amounts apply regardless of the destination country (Programme Guide 2026, p. 69).

### Additional considerations:
*   **Students with fewer opportunities:** You can receive a fixed top-up amount of **100 EUR** for a mobility of 5–14 days, or **150 EUR** for a mobility of 15–30 days (Programme Guide 2026, p. 70).
*   **Traineeships:** The specific top-up amount for traineeships does **not** apply to short-term physical mobility (Programme Guide 2026, p. 70).
*   **Travel support:** You may also be eligible for a travel grant depending on the distance to your destination and whether you use sustainable means of transport (Programme Guide 2026, pp. 71-72).

For the exact criteria regarding "fewer opportunities" or to confirm the final grant calculation, you should contact your home university's international office or your National Agency (SEPIE in Spain).

question: What counts as green travel in Erasmus+?
answer:
Green travel is defined as travel that uses **low emissions means of transport** for at least half of the round trip (Programme Guide 2026, p. 446).

The specific modes of transport that count as green travel include:
*   **Bus** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 446)
*   **Train** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 446)
*   **Bike** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 446)
*   **Car-pooling** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 446)

Additionally, traveling by **boat** is considered green travel if it is combined with other low-emissions means of transport (Programme Guide 2026, p. 446). 

The Erasmus+ programme promotes these sustainable transport modes to reduce the carbon and environmental footprint of mobility activities (Programme Guide 2026, p. 9, 47).

passages.text: In line with the principles of the ECHE, HEIs must promote environmentally friendly practices in all activities related to the Programme. question: Can I go on Erasmus+ without receiving an Erasmus+ grant?
answer:
Yes, you can participate in the Erasmus+ program without receiving a grant. These participants are known as **"zero-grant students"** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 66).

Here are the key details about this status:

*   **Definition:** Zero-grant students are mobile participants who do not receive an Erasmus+ mobility grant but fulfill all the criteria of the program and benefit from all the advantages of being an Erasmus+ student (Programme Guide 2026, p. 66).
*   **Benefits:** Even without the grant, you still benefit from the Erasmus+ framework, which includes not being charged fees for tuition, registration, or examinations at the receiving institution (Student Charter, "Your entitlements").

question: ¿Tengo que pagar matrícula en la universidad de destino?
answer:
No, **no tienes que pagar tasas de matrícula** en la universidad de destino.

Como estudiante de Erasmus+, tienes derecho a que no se te cobren tasas por enseñanza, matrícula, exámenes o acceso a laboratorios y bibliotecas durante tu periodo de movilidad (Erasmus+ Student Charter, "During the mobility period > Your entitlements").

*   **Pequeñas tasas:** Es posible que debas pagar importes reducidos por conceptos que también pagan los estudiantes locales, como seguros, asociaciones de estudiantes o el uso de materiales diversos como fotocopias o productos de laboratorio (ECHE Guidelines, p. 8).

question: Who has to approve the learning agreement, and when?
answer:
The Learning Agreement must be approved by **three parties**: the student, the sending institution (home university), and the receiving institution or organization (host university) (ECHE Guidelines, p. 15).

Regarding the timing:
*   **Before the mobility:** All three parties must digitally sign and approve the agreement before the student starts their period abroad (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Signing the learning agreement").
*   **Purpose:** This early approval is essential to ensure the automatic recognition of the credits earned abroad toward the student's home degree (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period").

The European Commission encourages these approvals to be done digitally (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Signing the learning agreement").

question: ¿Puedo cambiar las asignaturas de mi learning agreement cuando ya estoy en el destino?
answer:
Sí, puedes cambiar las asignaturas de tu *Learning Agreement* una vez que hayas llegado a tu destino, aunque estos cambios deben ser excepcionales (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Exceptional changes to the study programme").

Estas son las reglas principales para realizar los cambios:

*   **Plazo para solicitarlo:** Debes iniciar los cambios en un plazo de **cinco semanas** tras el inicio de cada semestre (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Exceptional changes to the study programme").
*   **Aprobación:** Los cambios deben ser acordados por las tres partes (tú, tu universidad de origen y la de destino) lo antes posible, en un plazo de **dos semanas** tras la solicitud (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Exceptional changes to the study programme").
*   **Procedimiento:** Los cambios no se hacen sobre el documento original, sino que se añaden en secciones específicas (Tablas A2 y B2) del acuerdo de aprendizaje digital (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Exceptional changes to the study programme").
*   **Validez:** Una vez que todas las partes firman la versión revisada, la universidad de origen está obligada a reconocer los créditos que apruebes según lo acordado (ECHE Guidelines, p. 16).

Es recomendable que consultes con la oficina de relaciones internacionales de tu universidad de origen para conocer si tienen algún procedimiento interno específico o plazos más cortos.

question: When must the host university send my transcript of records?
answer:
The host university (receiving institution) must normally send your transcript of records **within five weeks** after the publication of your results.

The specific details are as follows:
*   **Standard timeframe:** The transcript should be sent to you and your home university within a period stipulated in the inter-institutional agreement, which is normally within five weeks after the publication or proclamation of your results (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Transcript of Records at the receiving institution").
*   **Student entitlement:** According to the Erasmus+ Student Charter, you are entitled to receive this document, preferably in digital format, within five weeks of the publication of your results (Student Charter, "After the mobility period").
*   **Evaluation completion:** The guidelines for the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education also specify that this period should normally not be longer than five weeks after your evaluation is completed at the host institution (ECHE Guidelines, p. 21).

If there are delays, you should contact the person responsible for signing the transcript at your host university (ECHE Guidelines, p. 21). For the exact deadline applicable to your specific exchange, you can check with your home university's international office, as they manage the inter-institutional agreement.

question: If only my credits are transferred and not my grades, does it still count as automatic recognition?
answer:
Yes, it still counts as **automatic recognition** if only your credits are transferred and not your grades (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Does it count as full automatic recognition if...?").

According to the official guidelines, automatic recognition is achieved if:
* The credits to be earned were approved by all parties in the **Learning Agreement**.
* The credits were completed as confirmed by the **Transcript of Records**.
* You do not have to complete any additional courses, assignments, or exams to have those credits counted towards your degree (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Does it count as full automatic recognition if...?").

While the sending institution is encouraged to convert grades using the grade distribution information from the receiving institution, the core requirement for automatic recognition is the transfer of the total number of ECTS credits agreed upon without further assessment (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Automatic recognition at the sending institution").

question: How many ECTS credits is a normal full academic year?
answer:
A normal full academic year of full-time study consists of **60 ECTS credits** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 48).

According to the official guidelines:
*   **Standard workload:** In countries within the European Higher Education Area (EHEA), a full-time academic year is normally made up of educational components totalling 60 ECTS credits (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Educational components (Tables A and B)").
*   **Proportionality:** For mobility periods shorter than a full year, the number of credits in the learning agreement should be adjusted proportionally (Programme Guide 2026, p. 48).
*   **Expectations:** Students are expected to take 60 ECTS per year to avoid an unjustified prolongation of their studies (ECHE Guidelines, p. 8). While students should not be expected to earn more than 60 ECTS, they are allowed to exceed this number if they wish (ECHE Guidelines, p. 8).

question: What goes in Table A and Table B of the learning agreement?
answer:
In the Erasmus+ Learning Agreement for Studies, Tables A and B serve the following purposes:

*   **Table A:** You must list all educational components (courses, modules, laboratory work, thesis research, etc.) that you will carry out at the receiving (host) institution (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Educational components (Tables A and B)").
*   **Table B:** You must list the group of educational components at your sending (home) institution that will be replaced by the studies you complete abroad (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Educational components (Tables A and B)").

**Key points to remember:**
*   **No one-to-one correspondence required:** You do not need to match each individual course abroad to a specific course at your home university. Instead, a group of learning outcomes achieved abroad should replace a group of learning outcomes at your home institution (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Educational components (Tables A and B)").
*   **Automatic Recognition:** In Table B, the option for "Automatic Recognition" is selected by default. This confirms that the credits you earn abroad will be transferred and counted towards your degree without additional work or assessment (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Practical examples of how to fill in the tables in the digital learning agreement").
*   **Completeness:** You must fill in both tables thoroughly before your mobility begins (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Educational components (Tables A and B)").

question: Estudio en España y me voy a Alemania. ¿Qué tramo de beca me corresponde y de cuánto es?
answer:
Para una movilidad de estudios desde España a Alemania, te corresponde el **rango superior** de la beca (Higher range EU grant), ya que te desplazas desde un país del Grupo 2 a uno del Grupo 1 (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68).

Los detalles sobre la cuantía son los siguientes:

*   **Grupo de países:** España pertenece al **Grupo 2** (países con costes de vida medios) y Alemania al **Grupo 1** (países con costes de vida más altos) (Programme Guide 2026, pp. 67-68).
*   **Importe mensual:** El rango establecido por la Comisión Europea para este tipo de movilidad es de entre **348 y 674 EUR al mes** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68).
*   **Quién fija la cantidad exacta:** El importe final dentro de ese rango lo define la Agencia Nacional de cada país (en el caso de España, el **SEPIE**) o la propia universidad, basándose en criterios como la disponibilidad de cofinanciación o la demanda de becas (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68).

Para conocer la cifra exacta que recibirás este año, debes consultar la web del SEPIE o contactar con la oficina de relaciones internacionales de tu universidad.

question: I'm a Spanish student going to Poland for a semester and I have fewer opportunities. How much do I get per month?
answer:
As a student moving from Spain (Group 2) to Poland (Group 3), you are eligible for the "lower range" EU grant for your base monthly support, plus a top-up for having fewer opportunities (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68).

### Base Grant
Because you are moving from a country with medium living costs (Spain) to a country with lower living costs (Poland), you fall into the "lower range" category (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68). The EU sets the range for this category between **225 and 550 EUR per month** (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68).

### Top-up for Fewer Opportunities
As a student with fewer opportunities, you receive an additional top-up of **250 EUR per month** on top of your base grant (Programme Guide 2026, p. 68).

question: I did 5 months of Erasmus during my bachelor. Can I do a 9-month traineeship after graduating?
answer:
Yes, you can potentially do a 9-month traineeship as a recent graduate, provided you stay within the total limit of 12 months of Erasmus+ mobility for your bachelor's cycle.

Here are the key rules regarding your situation:

*   **Total Duration Limit:** You are allowed a maximum of 12 months of physical mobility per study cycle (in your case, the bachelor's cycle) (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).
*   **Counting Previous Mobility:** Any previous Erasmus+ mobility you completed during your bachelor's degree counts towards this 12-month limit (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54). Since you have already used 5 months, you have a maximum of 7 months of eligibility remaining for that cycle.
*   **Recent Graduate Traineeships:** Recent graduates can participate in a traineeship, but it must be completed within one year of obtaining your graduation (Programme Guide 2026, p. 55). Additionally, you must be selected by your higher education institution during your last year of study (Programme Guide 2026, p. 55).
*   **Important Note:** Because your previous 5 months count toward the 12-month limit, you would only have 7 months of eligibility remaining for a traineeship, not 9 months (Programme Guide 2026, p. 54).

Please note that your home university must opt-in to allow recent graduate traineeships, as they have the option to opt out of this programme (Programme Guide 2026, p. 55). You should contact your university's international office to confirm if they support recent graduate traineeships and to verify your remaining eligibility.

answer:

question: If I change courses during my stay, are the new courses still recognised automatically?
answer:
Changes to your courses are not automatically recognised unless they are formally agreed upon by all three parties (you, your sending institution, and your receiving institution) as a revised version of your Learning Agreement (ECHE Guidelines, p. 16).

While the Erasmus+ programme requires full automatic recognition of credits for successfully completed work, this applies to the courses originally agreed upon **or an agreed revised version of the Learning Agreement** (ECHE Guidelines, p. 16).

To ensure your new courses are recognised:

*   **Changes must be exceptional:** Changes to your study programme should be made only in exceptional cases (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Exceptional changes to the study programme").
*   **Formal approval is required:** Any changes must be agreed upon and validated by all three parties (you, your sending institution, and your receiving institution) (ECHE Guidelines, p. 16).
*   **Use the correct procedure:** You must indicate the changes in the designated tables (e.g., Tables A2, B2, C2) of your Learning Agreement. The original tables should not be modified; instead, the new tables create a revised version of the agreement (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Exceptional changes to the study programme").
*   **Respect deadlines:** You can typically initiate these changes within five weeks after the start of each semester, and they should be agreed upon by all parties as soon as possible, ideally within two weeks of your request (Learning Agreement guidelines, "Exceptional changes to the study programme").

If you have questions about the specific process for submitting these changes at your university, please contact your home university's international office.

question: Before I leave, what information am I entitled to and what do I have to sign?
answer:
Before you leave for your mobility period, you have specific entitlements regarding information and mandatory documents you must sign.

### What you must sign
*   **Grant Agreement:** You must sign a grant agreement with your sending institution (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period > Your obligations and duties").
*   **Learning Agreement:** You must sign a learning agreement with both your sending and receiving institutions. This document sets out the details of your activities abroad and is the basis for ensuring the automatic recognition of your mobility period (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period > Your obligations and duties"; ECHE Guidelines, p. 15).
*   **Online Language Assessment:** You are required to undergo an online language assessment through the Online Language Support (if available in the main language of instruction/work) after being selected (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period > Your obligations and duties").

### What you are entitled to receive
You are entitled to receive guidance and information on the following:
*   **Application and Mobility:** Information on the application process, the receiving institution, and the activities available during your mobility (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period > Your entitlements").
*   **Recognition:** Information on automatic recognition procedures and the grading system used by the receiving institution (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period > Your entitlements").
*   **Practical Support:** Information on obtaining insurance, finding housing, securing a visa (if required), and support facilities for those with special needs (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period > Your entitlements").
*   **Financial Support:** You are entitled to receive a pre-financing payment no later than the start date of your mobility period, provided the agreement has been signed by both parties or confirmation of arrival has been received (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period > Your entitlements").

*Note: You should ensure you have health insurance coverage for your stay abroad based on the information provided by your institution (Student Charter, "Before the mobility period > Your obligations and duties").*

passages.title: Erasmus+ Programme Guide 2026
passages.location: p. 43, HOW TO ACCESS ERASMUS+ HIGHER EDUCATION MOBILITY OPPORTUNITIES?
passages.section: HOW TO ACCESS ERASMUS+ HIGHER EDUCATION MOBILITY OPPORTUNITIES?
passages.text: The applicant organisation must be established in an EU Member State or third country associated to the Erasmus+ programme and have a higher education accreditation. It may either apply as an individual higher education institution, requiring an Erasmus Charter for Higher Education ( ECHE), or on behalf of a mobility consortium, requiring a consortium accreditation. Individual organisation accreditation – the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education Higher education institutions (HEIs) must have been awarded the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education (ECHE) before applying for a mobility project to their Erasmus+ National Agency. By signing the Erasmus Charter for Higher Education, higher education institutions commit to provide all the necessary support to mobile participants, including linguistic preparati on. Mobile participants can use the Erasmus+ Online Language Support (OLS) to improve their foreign language competences before and/or during mobility. Among other ECHE principles, the participating HEI must carry out mobility for the purpose of studying and teaching only within the framework of prior agreements between institutions and select prospective participants and award mobility grants in a fair, transparent, coherent, and documented way, in line with the provisions of its grant agreement with the National Agency. It should ensure such fair and transparent procedures throughout all stages of mobility and in the process of responding to queries/complaints from participants. It must ensure that no fees are charged in the case of credit mobility, to incoming mobile students for tuition, registration, examinations or access to laboratory and library facilities.

passages.title: Erasmus+ Programme Guide 2026
passages.location: pp. 46-47, INCLUSION AND DIVERSITY IN HIGHER EDUCATION MOBILITY
passages.section: INCLUSION AND DIVERSITY IN HIGHER EDUCATION MOBILITY
passages.text:
In order to make access to student and staff mobility as easy as possible, in line with the principles of the ECHE, HEIs must ensure equal and equitable access and opportunities to current and prospective participants from all backgrounds. This
means including participants with fewer opportunities, such as participants with physical, mental and health related conditions, students with children, student s who work or are professional athletes and students from all study fields underrepresented in mobility. Defining internal selection procedures that take into account equity and inclusion and assess applicants' merit and motivation holistically is essential in respecting this principle. Furthermore, HEIs are encouraged to establish built-in mobility opportunities, such as mobility windows within their curricula to help facilitate the participation of students from all study fields. In this regard, blended mobility can help offer additional opportunities that may be more suitable for some individuals or student groups. In this context, having in place inclusion officers within the higher education institutions helps address inclusion and diversity. Inclusion officers can for example help raise awareness, define stra tegies for communication and outreach, ensure adequate support throughout mobility in cooperation with relevant colleagues and help facilitate cooperation between relevant staff within the institution with expertise in the field of inclusion and divers ity.
